fullPassage: Why do AI chatbots sometimes state false information with unwavering confidence? A 2025 study conducted by researchers at OpenAI offers a counterintuitive answer: hallucination is not a random glitch but a predictable consequence of how these systems are trained. During training, a model is rewarded whenever it produces a specific answer—even an outright guess—while being given no credit for admitting uncertainty. Consequently, the model gradually learns that guessing carries less risk than acknowledging what it does not know, much as a student might prefer to write any answer on an exam rather than leave a blank space. According to the researchers, this tendency cannot be corrected simply by feeding the model more accurate data. What must change, they argue, is the very method by which AI systems are evaluated, so that expressions of uncertainty are treated as valid responses rather than failures. Until such reforms take hold, confident yet false statements are likely to remain an inherent feature of how artificial intelligence communicates with us.
